# docs(1684): mark the historical …-5772a26a-rocm 404 refs as superseded generated pins

**Implements:** issue #1684 residual (kanban t_b0af1c92) — the launcher vllm pin is GENERATED by
`scripts/engine_image.py` (`_tag_at`/`resolve`), not a literal, so the pin-update for #1684 is PR
#2274 itself (rocm cell → `prebuilt: true` over AMD's rocm/vllm base, regenerated pin
`3a4d82f5-16c7ff10-rocm` published, HTTP 200 in ghcr). No second pin PR is owed. The two remaining
`…-9be509b4` / `…-5772a26a` mentions on `main` live only in prose that records the measured five-day
HTTP 404 of the pre-#2274 pins, and are not pins at all.

## What changed

- **`openspec/changes/registry-liveness-dispatch/proposal.md`** — added a "superseded pins" note under
  the Why measurement: the recorded tags are *generated* pins, PR #2274 regenerates the rocm pin to
  the published `3a4d82f5-16c7ff10-rocm` (HTTP 200), and the historical `…-5772a26a-rocm` that 404''d
  for five days is superseded and no longer generated. The historical measurement is kept verbatim —
  rewriting it to a tag that never 404''d would assert a false measurement.
- **`tests/test_engine_build_collect.py`** — the #2259 regression docstring gains the same one-line
  freshening: the rocm tag is generated, regenerated by PR #2274 to the published `…-16c7ff10-rocm`,
  and the historical `…-5772a26a` is superseded. Test logic untouched.

## Decision (docs judgment)

Option (b): keep the historical 404 record and add the freshening note, rather than rewriting the
tags to the new published one — the old tags genuinely 404''d for five days, so renaming them would
falsify the recorded measurement. A reader who greps `…-5772a26a` now sees it is historical and
superseded, not a current pin.

## Verified

- `make lint`, `make check-docs`, `make check-wiring`, `make check-pr-authors`,
  `make check-pr-hygiene`, `make check-issue-bodies` all green at the pushed head (before merge; the
  docs gate is on the final head).
